requirements.requirement: node3 (behind node1/lan-a) can reach node4's HTTP service on TCP/8080 (behind node2/lan-b)
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.10.2.10:8080/ returns HTTP:200 both before any reboot (cmd-6171e57e2c0e414e, cmd-e6a750bee3814b5f) and after every subsequent router/host reboot (cmd-9c3ad78c84f24fa9 after node1 reboot, cmd-9f86030a880c4dba after node2 reboot, cmd-f0740471519b4cfd after node3 reboot, cmd-008aa0a937484c7d after node4 reboot).

requirements.requirement: All other traffic between lan-a and lan-b (ping, other ports such as tcp/22 and tcp/8081) remains refused
requirements.summary: ICMP echo to 10.10.2.10 fails (100% loss) and tcp/22 and tcp/8081 connections time out/refuse in the same probes that show tcp/8080 succeeding, both pre- and post-reboot (cmd-6171e57e2c0e414e shows HTTP:000 on 8081 and nc timeout on 22; cmd-9c3ad78c84f24fa9, cmd-9f86030a880c4dba, cmd-008aa0a937484c7d repeat this after each router/host reboot).

requirements.requirement: VyOS (node1) forward filter enforces default-drop with only established/related and a specific lan-a->lan-b tcp/8080 accept rule, persisted
requirements.summary: show firewall confirms rule 5 (established/related accept) and rule 10 (tcp/8080, 10.10.1.0/24->10.10.2.0/24 accept) with default-action drop, committed and saved (cmd-6ae7e5f3c6a940fa). nft ruleset shows an explicit trailing drop after the two rules both before and after node1's reboot (cmd-8645b7dd53d64eb4, cmd-039ed78c517346b6).

requirements.requirement: OPNsense (node2) interfaces/routing are correctly assigned and pf enforces a single pass rule for tcp/8080 lan-a->lan-b with default-deny otherwise, persisted
requirements.summary: opt1/opt2 interfaces are up with the correct addresses (cmd-efde9609565f4149), a route to lan-a exists via the transit gateway (cmd-0d250200b8ee41ff), and pfctl -sr shows only the tcp/8080 pass rule for 10.10.1.0/24->10.10.2.0/24 plus the interface-default block-drop rules (cmd-4daf5bd1f39942f4). Post-reboot verification (cmd-81abdedef6ff40bb) reproduces the same interfaces, routes, and pf ruleset.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Each node has a captured pre-reboot boot identity, an observed reboot trigger/ack (with an expected connection reset/timeout during the transition), a distinct post-reboot boot identity, and re-verified functional state: node1 (cmd-b28976a857974e9b, cmd-d6d5909eeebb4ece, cmd-f977946025e2414d, cmd-7e4f30715f33452a, cmd-039ed78c517346b6, cmd-9c3ad78c84f24fa9), node2 (cmd-b5778cbb1f924d69, cmd-ecd62d887bfa4c66, cmd-83ff49850f144638, cmd-81abdedef6ff40bb, cmd-9f86030a880c4dba), node3 (cmd-51019df370654233, cmd-25f9ae2c3cf147c2, cmd-d981078951a34e5f, cmd-f0740471519b4cfd), node4 (cmd-5fdf7c81f0154ea1, cmd-025e497a587046e8, cmd-bdd63a109ce74e37, cmd-a96eedb59b684f0b, cmd-bc731cd4c37c40b8, cmd-008aa0a937484c7d). The fixed global boot-identity snapshots independently corroborate all four boot-id/boottime changes versus before_prepare.

overall_summary: The executor established a transit path (VyOS node1 <-> OPNsense node2) with static addressing for lan-a/lan-b/transit, added a VyOS forward-filter (default-drop + established/related + tcp/8080 lan-a->lan-b accept) and an OPNsense pf pass rule scoped to the same flow, and directly demonstrated node3 reaching node4:8080 over HTTP while ping and other ports (22, 8081) remained refused. All four nodes were individually rebooted with captured pre-reboot boot identities, an observed disruption, distinct post-reboot boot identities, and re-verified interface/route/firewall state plus continued correct HTTP/deny behavior after each reboot, satisfying the restart-evidence protocol. Hygiene is good: discovery-phase test IP assignments were bounded and reverted, and the only residue is an ephemeral, non-persistent test HTTP server and its temp files on node4 that the executor itself introduced to enable verification.
limitations: The HTTP service on node4:8080 was stood up by the executor as an ad hoc python3 http.server rather than being a pre-existing managed service; it is not persisted via a system service manager, so it required manual restart after node4's reboot (cmd-bc731cd4c37c40b8), which is a plausible but unverified assumption about what 'the HTTP service node4 serves' was meant to be.

The OPNsense 'configctl routes configure' command returned an error ('Action not allowed or missing') even though the resulting route was present in netstat -rn; the evidence does not fully explain which action caused the route to appear, though the final state is directly observed and correct.

operational_hygiene.summary: Topology-discovery mutations on node1/node2/node3/node4 (temporary 172.16.x IPs on eth1/eth2/vtnet1/vtnet2/enp8s0, cmd-783a19e0e3bd481f, cmd-dc9d8c2d73104da2, cmd-64a5475d9c2048b3, cmd-a670ca45a8764c43, cmd-f8607407aa6a4871, cmd-e145e2d756c04853, cmd-f3045af0cda64646) were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted before final configuration (cmd-89edf1bfb144413c, cmd-ac9f5b4c1daa413f, cmd-6d4a50108eef498d, cmd-07321edda4c34187), so they warrant minimal penalty. A failed VyOS CLI syntax probe (cmd-2b3230c7970c4c09) made no state change. The only lasting residue is an executor-created ephemeral python3 http.server on node4 (cmd-82cbae6580804dbf, restarted after reboot at cmd-bc731cd4c37c40b8), leaving /tmp/http8080.log and /tmp/http8080.pid and a non-persistent listener; this was necessary to have any HTTP service on 8080 to test against but is not managed via a persistent unit and was not cleaned up, which is a minor unaddressed residue.
